### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c064d3a24610508918ccefd1e0a94b6a759448d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `30344b92cd008d8e421e7e27fd22bdf064634113` — the merge of head `6f15ad27f7406f90547af738b90b99797147bbb3` into base `c064d3a24610508918ccefd1e0a94b6a759448d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 30344b92cd008d8e421e7e27fd22bdf064634113 && git checkout 30344b92cd008d8e421e7e27fd22bdf064634113
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c064d3a24610508918ccefd1e0a94b6a759448d9 6f15ad27f7406f90547af738b90b99797147bbb3 && git checkout -B drift-repro c064d3a24610508918ccefd1e0a94b6a759448d9 && git merge --no-ff 6f15ad27f7406f90547af738b90b99797147bbb3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c064d3a24610508918ccefd1e0a94b6a759448d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f15ad27f7406f90547af738b90b99797147bbb3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/save-notice-placement.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/save-notice-node.test.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts (`triggerTypeToHookEvents`, `start()`'s array-form warn-and-return), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin-extension-api.ts (`deriveTriggerBinding`), packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts (the array-form finding), packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts (`INERT_CONDITION_NODE_TYPES`, `FALLIBLE_NODE_TYPES` and their two use sites) and its test, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/save-notice-node.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`suspendedRunStore: 'auto'`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`suspendedRuns` is not a read-through cache, #13617), packages/services/service-automation/src/suspended-run-store.ts (`ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore`, JSON columns), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/save-notice-approval-round-trip.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`decide`, the stranded exit), packages/types/src/stranded-decision.ts, .changeset/28786-save-notice-follow-ups.md

Inputs read: card #28786 (body; comments 6562950408 triage, 6562970286 claim, 6563740409 os-dev-report); PR #28805 body and 6-file list; the net diff `git diff 56fdd563 6f15ad27` (6 files, +265 −5; the branch restarted on main at `56fdd563`, five commits, no merge); the check-runs on the head at two reads. Judged on the tree, not the PR body's account.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`saveNoticePlacementRefusals` keeps its verdict and changes only the sentence for an array `triggerType`.** Right. The early return is untouched (`typeof trigger === 'string' && SAVE_NOTICE_TRIGGER.test(trigger.trim())`), so the accept set is byte-for-byte what `main` accepts; an array still falls to the refusal, now spelled as the shape the author wrote. The array form is unsupported and never binds (`start()` in `record-change-trigger.ts` logs and returns for a joined event that maps to no hook; `deriveTriggerBinding` routes it there for that purpose; `validate-flow-trigger-readiness` already flags it), so "not supported and never binds, so no write waits on the run" is a true statement about the consumer. The advice — ONE trigger type, `'record-after-write'` for create-or-update — is the trigger's own prescription for the array case and is the right one for a `save_notice`, whose write is a create or an update. The string case and the missing case keep their previous sentence verbatim. No tracker number in the runtime string (the `#3457` cite is in the code comment).
2. **No published surface moves.** Right: no export, type, schema shape, JSON Schema or generated artifact changes; the file list carries no `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/` or manifest file, and none is owed for a refusal-text change.
3. **Lint: `save_notice` joins `INERT_CONDITION_NODE_TYPES` and `FALLIBLE_NODE_TYPES`.** Right, both by reading the executor as the lists' headers demand. `save-notice-node.ts` parses `message` only through `SaveNoticeConfigSchema` (a `strictObject`; `condition` on the node config would itself be refused at parse) and never reads `condition` — the word does not occur in the file — so a `condition` on the node is inert and `flow-inert-node-condition` (use site at line 1228) is the right finding. The executor returns `success: false` on data alone at exactly the three lines the row cites (67: no channel; 94: every hole rendered empty; 104: the channel's own refusal), so `flow-loop-body-uncontained` (use site at line 1763) is the right warning for one in a loop body with no `try_catch`. Both rows are pinned (inert: 1 finding with the node named; fallible: `n12` added to the sweep's expected list).
4. **No governed surface** in the file list; head repo is the base repo; 270 changed lines; draft. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28786-save-notice-follow-ups.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/lint: patch`. Both names match their `package.json`.

- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset. Right: nothing is accepted or refused differently (①1), no key, value or requirement moves, no `(narrowing)` arm, so no BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both. Right: a refusal sentence and lint classifications change nothing an author can write. `none` must grade every entry `patch` and move no `authorable-surface/` baseline — both hold.
- `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` gains only a test and publishes nothing from it: correctly absent from the changeset. `@objectstack/service-automation` is read, not changed. `Check Changeset` is `success` on both runs at the last read.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Does the round-trip test drive a persisted `SuspendedRunStore` path?** Yes, read in the tree. `AutomationServicePlugin` with `suspendedRunStore` unset takes `'auto'` (`plugin.ts` 192, 1834–1851), which builds `ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore` over `sys_automation_run` on the kernel's data engine; the test registers the approvals package's objects, `syncSchemas()` creates the table under a real `SqlDriver`, and `RecordChangeTriggerPlugin` is real. The engine's in-memory `suspendedRuns` map is "NOT a read-through cache sitting in front of the store" (#13617), so the decision resumes off the row. The test's own evidence confirms it: it reads the `paused` row's `context_json` (no `saveNotice.set`), and the resumed node's refusal is the **no-channel** sentence (`this run holds no record write to answer`), which only a context without a `set` function produces — a leg resumed from the live in-memory channel would have carried the trigger's **closed-channel** sentence instead. Then the pause row is consumed and the `run_` history row is `failed` with the node's error. The dev's ablation (the no-channel `refuseNode` replaced by success, test red, restored by blob) is the coverage pin; it was made on `service-automation`'s built `dist`, the file the test resolves, which is the honest target. Item 2 of the card is met.
- **The stranded-decision `RESUME_FAILED` pin — right, or a defect to escalate?** Right as pinned, and not a defect of this PR or of the save-notice design. `stranded-decision.ts` records the maintainer-ruled posture: an approval decision finalises first (request row terminal, audit written, mirrored status advanced) and only then resumes the run; when the resume fails, the writes stand, the run is stranded, and `decide` throws the 500-class `RESUME_FAILED` carrying `strandedDecisionDetails` — deliberately, so a recorded decision whose flow never advanced is never reported as "did not happen". A `save_notice` on the resumed leg is the #28251 design's "refused by name, never dropped silently" (the alternative — the node silently succeeding after the answer was sent — is exactly what #28251 refused), so the test reads two existing contracts meeting and pins what they do. The test asserts `finalized: true, decision: 'approve', runId` and that the listener heard nothing more, which is the whole of the truthful-throw ruling. **Escalated, as a finding to file, not a change here:** an author can publish a flow with a `save_notice` downstream of a suspending node (`approval`, `wait`, `screen`); the parse cannot see suspension, so every decision on such a flow strands its run. That is a metadata-authoring trap in PD#10's sense, with its evidence (this test), and the remedy is a static lint finding (a `save_notice` reachable only through a suspending node), which the dev noted in `out_of_scope_findings` but did not file under "new gates default to no". The seat should file it as its own card (p3, `packages/lint`); a lint finding is a repo gate only if wired as one, and a `warn`-class finding needs no gate ruling.
- **Deviation 1 (ablation on `dist`, restored by blob).** Accepted; the restore is verified and the working tree is not what is reviewed here.
- **Deviation 2 (terminal row's `node_id` is the suspension node, not the failing one, so not pinned).** Accepted; the error text names the failing node, which is what the test reads.
- **Test wall time.** The single `it` declares a 20 s ceiling; no measured wall is reported. A file over 10 s of wall becomes its lane's card unless it declares a measured budget — the dev should state the measured wall in the report or the file header (a note, not a finding; Test Core on the head is the measurement).
- `open_questions: []`. Nothing else is flagged.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/save-notice-placement.ts`** — against the trigger grammar it cites and the three shapes an author can write:

- String trigger in the grammar: accepted, unchanged. String trigger outside it (`'record-after-delete'`, `'schedule'`, `'api'`): refused with the previous sentence, unchanged, and `save-notice-node.test.ts` keeps those pins.
- Array trigger: refused with the new sentence. Tried to break it: (a) `['record-after-create', 'record-after-update']` — the exact shape the pin writes; the sentence quotes it, says it never binds, and the advice (`'record-after-write'`) is the one token that covers both members; (b) `['record-after-create', 'record-after-delete']` — still refused; the advice is still right for a `save_notice` (its write is never a delete) and matches the trigger's own warning text; (c) an empty array or a non-string member — the `trigger.map` over `String(t)` renders `[]` or the stringified member; nothing throws inside the `FlowSchema` parse, which is the property that matters (a throw there would escape `safeParse`). (d) The array branch is checked before the string branch, so a string can never fall into it. (e) Index anchoring is unchanged from the peer arms.
- The verdict is unchanged, which is the card's ⛔ line and the `Clause-②: no` claim; ①1 reads it off the untouched early return.
- The pin asserts the issue code and path (`['custom', ['nodes', 1, 'type']]`), the new sentence verbatim, and the absence of the old "no record trigger" phrase.

No finding on the hits file.

Lane remainder, read for ③ and not reviewed here: the integration test and the lint rows hold against the code they cite (①3, ③). One note for the lane seat: the test's header says a store that "started keeping (or re-binding) the channel" is caught here — true for `set` (the assertion is `typeof stored.saveNotice?.set === 'undefined'`), while `locale` surviving is allowed by the test, which is the intended shape.

No must-fix, no should-fix. One escalation (③): file the authoring-trap lint finding as its own card.

**VERDICT: PASS**
